chunk_text: Federal ordinary-income brackets for a taxpayer filing as single: 10% on income from $0 to $11,600; 12% on income from $11,600 to $47,150; 22% on income from $47,150 to $100,525; 24% on income from $100,525 to $191,950; 32% on income from $191,950 to $243,725; 35% on income from $243,725 to $609,350; 37% on income above $609,350. Brackets are marginal, so only the income falling inside a band is taxed at that band's rate; reaching the 37% bracket at $609,350 does not retax the first $11,600. All figures are from the synthetic TY2026 schedule used by this fixture and are illustrative only.

Marginal versus effective rate for single filers: the marginal rate is the rate on the next dollar earned, while the effective rate is total liability divided by total income. A single taxpayer whose top band is 35% will always show an effective rate below that, because the lower bands are taxed at their own rates first. Withholding tables approximate the effective rate, which is why a raise mid-year often under-withholds. All figures are from the synthetic TY2026 schedule used by this fixture and are illustrative only.

The standard deduction for single is $14,600, subtracted from adjusted gross income to reach taxable income before the bracket ladder is applied. Itemising replaces this amount rather than adding to it, so itemised totals below $14,600 leave the taxpayer worse off. Taxpayers aged 65 or over, or blind, add $1,950 per qualifying condition. All figures are from the synthetic TY2026 schedule used by this fixture and are illustrative only.

Alternative Minimum Tax for single: the AMT exemption is $85,700, phasing out at 25 cents per dollar of alternative minimum taxable income above $609,350. AMTI is computed by adding back preference items - most commonly the state and local tax deduction, incentive stock option spread, and private-activity bond interest. The taxpayer pays the greater of regular tax and tentative minimum tax, never both. All figures are from the synthetic TY2026 schedule used by this fixture and are illustrative only.

Long-term capital-gains thresholds for single: a 0% rate applies to taxable income up to $47,025, 15% from there to $518,900, and 20% above $518,900. The holding period that separates long-term from short-term treatment is more than one year; short-term gains are taxed at ordinary rates. A separate 3.8% net investment income tax applies above the NIIT threshold and stacks on top of the capital-gains rate. All figures are from the synthetic TY2026 schedule used by this fixture and are illustrative only.

Summary for a preparer reviewing a return: Estimated tax payments are due quarterly on April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15 of the following year. The safe-harbour rule waives the underpayment penalty for a taxpayer who pays at least 90% of the current year's liability or 100% of the prior year's, rising to 110% when prior-year adjusted gross income exceeded $150,000. All figures are from the synthetic TY2026 schedule used by this fixture and are illustrative only.

Summary for a preparer reviewing a return: Withholding is reconciled on the annual return: amounts withheld by an employer are a credit against total liability, not a separate tax. A refund means the credit exceeded the liability, which is an interest-free loan to the government rather than a rebate. All figures are from the synthetic TY2026 schedule used by this fixture and are illustrative only.
